clue.text: Daughter is chased by pig that's let out

indicators.note: being chased by means coming behind, so the gorging part follows

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in genealogies
to pig is to eat greedily, to gorge

explanation.surface: A daughter pursued by an escaped pig through the farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pig' reads as the animal that escaped, but it is a verb here: to pig out is to GORGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgorge is to discharge or release something held inside, so it means to let out.

clue.text: Ready to cheat mum

parts.note: to do someone is slang for to swindle them
mum as in 'keep mum' means silent, as is sh

explanation.surface: Prepared to deceive one's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is British slang for cash, as is DOSH; 'mum' is silence, not mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British terms for money, cash in hand.

clue.text: Small quantity in narrow opening

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
a lot is a quantity, as a batch at auction

explanation.surface: A little bit poked through a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot is a thin aperture, such as one for coins in a machine.

clue.text: US state with mines mostly worked out?

parts.note: mines produce ore

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: gone means exhausted, used up

explanation.surface: A US state whose mines are largely exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is a state on the Pacific coast of the USA.

clue.text: Suggestion to ditch leader unfortunately blocked by eccentric toff with the ability to speak unknown languages

definitions.text: the ability to speak unknown languages

indicators.note: being blocked means having something stuck in the middle, so the toff sits inside
unfortunately signals the remaining letters fall out badly, so they are scrambled
ditching the leader drops the opening letter of suggestion
eccentric means odd, so toff's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dotty toff gets in the way of a suggestion from a gifted linguist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' and 'eccentric' are both anagram signals: the suggestion without its S is scrambled, and the scrambled toff sits in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the apostles were granted the miraculous power to speak languages they had never learned.

clue.text: Here's a surprise about the French overture from Ravel? It's not an overture

indicators.note: about means going around, so the boo wraps the other letters

parts.note: BOO is what you shout to give someone a surprise
LE is French for the

indicators.note: the overture of a word is its opening, so this takes the first letter of Ravel

explanation.surface: A question about some surprising French overture by Ravel, answered by saying it is not one at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel's Bolero is a stand-alone orchestral piece, not an overture, so the closing remark defines it with a wink; 'overture' is also used in the wordplay for the first letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravel's best-known orchestral work is a single-movement piece built on one repeated rhythm, not an opening to an opera.

clue.text: Little item in proposal not entirely complete, not entirely pure

indicators.note: in means the little item goes inside
not complete means missing its last letter

parts.note: an offer is a proposal
a whit is a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A small item in a proposal that is half finished and not quite above board.
explanation.walkthrough: OFFE (offer without its last letter) has WHIT placed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-white is a colour that is very nearly but not quite pure white.

clue.text: More space arranged around old game venue

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround old
arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Extra space set out around an old venue for games.
explanation.walkthrough: MORE SPACE rearranged gives ESCAPEROM, which goes around O.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape room is a themed room where players solve puzzles to get out against the clock.

clue.text: Green picked up correspondence — nothing to replace a study of the sea

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted, read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: eco means environmentally friendly, green

indicators.note: to replace means the nothing takes the place of the a

parts.note: an analogy is a correspondence between things
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An environmentalist collecting letters as a study of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' sounds like a homophone but reverses ECO; in ANALOGY the second A becomes O, giving ANOLOGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanology is the scientific study of the oceans, another name for oceanography.

clue.text: Rung number? Most of class engaged, possibly

parts.note: a spoke is a rung of a ladder or chair

indicators.note: most of means one letter short of the whole word for class

parts.note: a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A puzzling list: a rung, a number, a school class, and a guess about engagement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone already taken, as by a fiancé, is spoken for; the 'possibly' admits the phrase also covers reserved things.

clue.text: Dismissed old fellow leading second eleven to finish exhausted?

indicators.note: leading means coming in front, so these letters precede the rest

parts.note: run out is a way a batsman is dismissed in cricket
a cricket or football team has eleven players

explanation.surface: A cricketer run out as an old hand captains the second eleven, ending the match worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is run out when the ball breaks the wicket before they reach the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: To run out of steam is to lose energy and come to a halt, like a steam engine.

clue.text: Feminine reserve about husband's file

parts.note: F is the grammatical abbreviation for feminine

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reserve goes round the husband

parts.note: ice means a cold, distant reserve of manner
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife's reticence over her husband's personal records.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiche is a microfiche, a sheet of film holding a document, the kind of record kept in an archive.

clue.text: Set subsequently including father has to fail

parts.note: the sun sets, or goes down

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the word for subsequently wraps father

parts.note: then means afterwards, subsequently
PA is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A father, it seems, is bound to fail eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: GO DOWN THE PAN is British slang for to be wasted or ruined, as if flushed down a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase pictures something flushed away, so it means a plan or venture collapsing.

clue.text: Heartbroken to block dubious trade in pyramids

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, inside the other word
dubious means shady, suggesting the letters of trade are jumbled

parts.note: the word splits as heart plus broken: the letters of heart, broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A heartbroken trader caught up in a shady trade in pyramids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartbroken' is read as HEART broken, so its letters are rearranged to TRAHE; this sits inside TEDRA, the anagram of trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrahedron is a solid with four triangular faces, a triangular pyramid; tetrahedra is its plural.

clue.text: One amongst majority to get prominent about source of ugly work with cosmetics?

indicators.note: amongst means placed inside the majority word

parts.note: most means the majority
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to rise is to become prominent

explanation.surface: A beautician wondering how to treat a prominent ugly spot.
explanation.walkthrough: MOIST (I in MOST), then U, then RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisturise is to apply cream to the skin, a basic cosmetic routine.

clue.text: Love to have sex, not about to retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
not means the following item is left out

parts.note: to score is slang for to have sex
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A lover keen on sex but not willing to back off.
explanation.walkthrough: SCORE without C (circa, 'about') leaves SORE, which retreats to EROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, so his name stands for love itself.

clue.text: Star culture mostly irregular of form

indicators.note: irregular means not in order, so these letters are rearranged
mostly means all but the last letter of culture

explanation.surface: A celebrity culture that is mostly erratic in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: STAR and CULTUR (culture without its last letter) are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Structural describes the shape or framework of something, so it concerns its form.

clue.text: They'll carefully select social media users getting variable for time

indicators.note: getting means the word receives a new letter
for means instead of, so one letter takes another's place

parts.note: tweeters post on Twitter
Z is a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: Social media users picking carefully, with a variable standing in for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweezers are small pincers used to pick out tiny things such as hairs or splinters.

clue.text: Argument about curtailment of embroidery to finish church feature

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the row goes round the rest

parts.note: a row is a noisy argument

indicators.note: curtailment means cutting off the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: sewing is needlework such as embroidery
to do something can mean to finish it, as in 'that's done'

explanation.surface: A quarrel over shortened needlework, to be finished before church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' for finish is as in 'the job is done'; the needlework loses only its final G.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose window is a circular stained-glass window with radiating tracery, typical of Gothic cathedrals.

clue.text: Scent trace of oranges in country near Australia

indicators.note: in means the trace goes inside the country's letters

parts.note: PNG is Papua New Guinea, Australia's northern neighbour

indicators.note: a trace is the smallest hint, here the first letter of oranges

explanation.surface: Detecting a whiff of oranges in a Pacific nation.
explanation.walkthrough: A pong is British slang for a bad smell; the clue's neutral 'Scent' covers it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pong is informal British for an odour, usually an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Keen on repeating second half, considering everything

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: repeating means the latter half of the keen-on word is said again

explanation.surface: Someone keen to repeat the second half after weighing everything.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for 'in total', meaning taken as a whole.

clue.text: Dislike about university's hint to suppress one crime? What's cooking, seriously?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the dislike goes round university

parts.note: to hate is to dislike strongly
U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so the hint wraps the rest

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or hint
I is the Roman numeral one
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Someone who hates hints of crime at a university asks what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's cooking?' usually means 'what's happening?'; taken seriously it asks about the food, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Haute cuisine is elaborate high-class French cookery, cooking taken at its most serious.

clue.text: Passing comment? Nothing had an effect

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
something bit when it took effect, as when cuts bite

explanation.surface: A remark that came to nothing, then had an impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' is death, not walking by; an obit is a newspaper obituary.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a notice commenting on someone who has died.

clue.text: German composer I overlooked successfully

indicators.note: overlooked means missed out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: Kurt Weill was the German composer of The Threepenny Opera

explanation.surface: A German composer's work I passed over had gone well.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something well is to do it in a satisfactory, accomplished manner.

clue.text: Motivation beginning to recede in downmarket bar

indicators.note: in means placed inside the bar's letters

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar

indicators.note: the beginning of recede is its first letter

explanation.surface: Losing one's motivation in a seedy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is ambition or energy that pushes someone on, a synonym of motivation.

clue.text: Feel something of a blow to experience second sight thus?

definitions.text: Feel something of a blow to experience second sight thus?

parts.words: Feel something of a blow to experience second sight thus?
parts.note: a knock on the head makes your vision blur into two images, a literal second sight

explanation.walkthrough: Second sight normally means clairvoyance; here it is read as seeing everything twice over after being hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to have double vision, as when dazed or drunk.

clue.text: Discriminating person is engaged in a purchase

indicators.note: engaged in means held inside, so is sits within the purchase word

parts.note: to get something can mean to buy it

explanation.surface: A discerning buyer making a purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discriminating' suggests a person of taste; it means one who discriminates unfairly.
explanation.definitionFit: An ageist treats people unfairly because of how old they are, a form of prejudice.

clue.text: Wrong to besiege Troy without end

indicators.note: besieging means surrounding, so the wrong word encircles Troy

parts.note: immoral means morally wrong
t is the abbreviation for troy, the weight system

explanation.surface: The Greeks were wrong to besiege Troy, a war without end.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy is not the city here but troy weight, abbreviated t.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immortal never dies, existing endlessly.
